title: On-Ice Stick & Puck
notes: Stick & Puck session (scheduled 2-hour window; actual high-quality goalie exposure ~70–80 mins before meaningful fatigue became apparent; exact total duration on ice is unknown and not stored as an exact figure). Movement/positioning: Composed, kept things simple, moving around the net well, only a couple instances off angles, movement good particularly earlier in session, full effort, no pain. Performance context: Monday shooter skill level lower than prior Friday, limited defensive support; with roughly 20 min remaining allowed ~5 goals while making several exceptional saves. Final ~10 min became materially different with essentially no defense and getting shelled (not directly comparable, no standalone KPI). Notable observation: exceptional glove save while extended / nearly in splits ('I made a glove save that had everybody freaking shocked' - defender had strong reaction, shooter asked about sticky gloves; stored as notable athlete-reported observation, not objective rating). Post-session state: legs tired, not sore, no pain, general feeling positive, glad he attended. Interpretation boundary: evidence shows quality remained high for substantial portion followed by accumulated fatigue and changed late environment; no learned pattern created.
